quote: I'm just thinking about it, see how much if I even go forward with it, how much I'm looking at.
stewart_read: This is the emotional-anchor question and customer gave a thin, exploratory answer; rep did not probe deeper (why solar, what triggered the form-fill) before moving straight to prior-design question.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged that pressing further wasn't needed since bill pain surfaced naturally later via the bill amount and summer usage discussion.
coaching_implication: Spend 30-60 seconds expanding 'thinking about it' into a concrete motivator (bill, environment, resale) before moving on — deeper anchor material to use at bill flip and button-up.

stewart_read: Bill amount captured cleanly and quickly (within 90 seconds), meeting the 4-minute bill-anchor target.
coaching_implication: Capture was fast and clean — the miss is not in capture but in flip (see anchor_use).

quote: K. Yeah. Definitely. You're probably spending a lot in the summertime.
stewart_read: Rep references the bill's seasonal spike but frames it as an observation about usage, not as emotional alignment against the utility (no 'that bill is the real cost' framing).
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deliberately saving the emotional flip for the closer per setter_scope_discipline, treating this as informational handoff only.
coaching_implication: This was the moment to flip: 'that's money ComEd is taking from you every summer — let's see how much of that we can get back' would align bill pain to action.

quote: You cannot just send it to me through email or something?
stewart_read: Rep held the hard rule correctly ('we like to go through it with you') but did not use the objection-inversion flip available for the underlying reluctance to meet.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's response was schema-compliant enough (held line, offered phone alternative) — the objection was resolved procedurally without needing a full inversion.
coaching_implication: Rebuttal held correctly; inversion is optional polish here, not a hard miss.

quote: Yeah. Give me a phone call, Barry, because, I mean k. My my plans keep changing and everything.
stewart_read: Customer flags unstable plans right as he agrees to the time slot — a soft fragility signal on whether the 1PM slot will actually hold.
coaching_implication: Should have been flagged explicitly for the closer, e.g., confirming the 1PM slot is firm given his changing schedule, or building in a reschedule-friendly note.

quote: Either way, you're gonna send me a copy on everything. Right?
stewart_read: Button-up covered day/time and phone number but never ran the full 'is that fair?' handshake or the no-driving/one-hour-block language before the call wrapped.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have felt the call was short and simple enough that the full button-up script was unnecessary given cooperative customer.
coaching_implication: Add the 'blocked an hour, is that fair?' handshake even on smooth calls — it's the show-rate predictor, not just formality.
